newsitem.title: PERU: SOCCER-PERU BEATS U.S. ON THREE SECOND-HALF GOALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PERU BEATS U.S. ON THREE SECOND-HALF GOALS.

text.p: The United States suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat to unheralded Peru on Wednesday in an international soccer friendly.
Even without exerting themselves fully, Peru completely dominated the game and made the United States look like the second-rate team they brought to South America.

With their key players absent due to club duties and contractual wrangling, the U.S. replacement team could offer few attacking possibilities and were frequently at a loss to cope with Peru's neat passing.
Peru, after squandering a slew of chances in the first half, took the lead in the 33rd minute when Roberto Palacios coolly side-footed home from 12 meters.
But a Peruvian defensive lapse just before halftime allowed a U.S. equaliser when Alvaro Barco fluffed a clearance and gifted American Dario Brose a tap-in goal.
In the second half, Peru's dominance bore fruit as Percy Olivares, Paolo Maldonado and Nolberto Solano all scored against a hapless U.S. defence that left the home side too much space to shoot.

Olivares earned his goal in the 67th minute by surging forward to finish off a flowing Peruvian attack. Then Maldonado found himself free after sloppy defending to fire the ball home in the 73rd minute from the edge of the box.
Finally, in the 83rd minute, Solano put the game beyond the reach of the tired U.S. team with a blast from 20 meters into the corner of the goal.
